help.text:
[Basic use]
Paste a URL into the "URL" field (press Enter to start right away), or click "Import batch" and choose a .txt list
(one URL per line; lines starting with # are comments; duplicate URLs are skipped; items are downloaded one after another).

[Cancel and info]
Click "Cancel" while downloading to stop. "Get video info" shows the title and the qualities actually available.

[Quality]
Choosing 720P means "up to 720P"; if the video has nothing that low, the lowest available quality is used.

[Playlists]
When you paste a YouTube URL that includes a playlist, you are asked before the download starts whether to download just the video or the whole playlist.
Choosing the whole playlist creates a folder whose name you can set; if left blank it is named "PlaylistN" automatically.
Checking "Number playlist items" on the right prefixes file names with 01, 02, … (whole playlists only).

[Cookies]
If a site needs you to be logged in, export cookies.txt with a browser extension and click "Import Cookies.txt" (it takes priority).
For safety, the Cookies.txt path is not remembered; you must choose it again every time you start the program.
You can also pick a browser on the right to read its cookies directly (recent Chrome / Edge versions may not be decryptable).

[Advanced]
"Remember downloads (skip duplicates)" records downloaded videos in config/archive.txt and skips them next time.

[Download acceleration]
With "Enable download acceleration" checked, yt-dlp's -N downloads several fragments at once (4 / 8 / 16).
It only works for fragmented streams (such as m3u8/HLS and DASH manifests). Ordinary single-file downloads, including most YouTube videos, do not get faster,
and for those the progress bar merges into one automatically. Too many fragments may get you throttled or an HTTP 429 from the site.

dl.msg.no_engine: yt-dlp was not found. Run pip install yt-dlp, or put yt-dlp.exe in the program folder.
dl.msg.reload:
YouTube asked to reload the page. This may be caused by an outdated yt-dlp, player verification or your login state.
Click "Check for updates" first; if it still fails, import a fresh YouTube Cookies.txt.
dl.msg.ffmpeg: FFmpeg is missing or can't run. Put ffmpeg.exe in the program folder, or add FFmpeg to the system PATH, then try again.
dl.msg.outdated: The download failed because yt-dlp is out of date. Click "Check for updates" first.
dl.msg.http412: Bilibili returned HTTP 412 (anti-bot check). Log in to bilibili.com in your browser first; you may also need to re-import Cookies.txt. Then click "Check for updates" to update yt-dlp.
dl.msg.rate_limit: The server says there were too many requests (HTTP 429). Try again later; if subtitles are on, reduce the number of subtitle languages.
dl.msg.cookie_dpapi: Failed to read cookies: Windows DPAPI can't decrypt the browser's cookies. Export Cookies.txt with a browser extension instead.
dl.msg.cookie: Failed to read or parse cookies. Make sure the browser is completely closed, or import Cookies.txt instead.
dl.msg.login: This video requires a login, age verification or a bot check. Import a Cookies.txt from a logged-in session and try again.
dl.msg.js_runtime: yt-dlp couldn't find a usable JavaScript runtime, so some YouTube videos may fail to parse. Install Deno (or Node.js) and click "Check for updates" first.
dl.msg.format: No quality or format matches your choice. Pick "Default" quality and try again.
dl.msg.unsupported: yt-dlp doesn't support this URL. Check that the URL is complete.
dl.msg.unavailable: The video isn't available (it may be deleted, private or region-restricted).
dl.info.timeout: Reading the video info timed out. Check your network or try again later.
ffmpeg.missing.head: FFmpeg was not found; downloads (merging video and audio, converting) need it.

ffmpeg.missing.or_path: Or add FFmpeg to the system PATH, then try again.
ffmpeg.missing.win: The FFmpeg site mainly offers source code; Windows builds usually link to third-party builds (such as gyan.dev or BtbN). Choose one in the "Windows" section of the download page.
ffmpeg.missing.mac: On macOS you can also install it with Homebrew: brew install ffmpeg
ffmpeg.missing.linux: You can also install ffmpeg with your Linux distribution's package manager.
